description.value: The study assessed changes in brain reward reactivity to visual food cues before and after an 8-week low energy diet followed by a 2-year weight maintenance period, and examined associations between changes in brain activation and protein intake, anthropometrics, insulin resistance and eating behaviour.

spans.text: The objective was to assess the effects of a weight loss and subsequent weight maintenance period comprising two diets differing in protein intake, on brain reward reactivity to visual food cues.

value: We hypothesized that participants with higher protein intake had reduced brain reactivity to food cues after 2 years compared to participants with moderate protein intake.

spans.text: We hypothesized that participants with higher protein intake had reduced brain reactivity to food cues after 2 years compared to participants with moderate protein intake.

description.value: Participants underwent an 8-week low energy diet followed by a 2-year weight maintenance period with either moderate-protein or high-protein dietary guidelines. Participants were randomized into two dietary intervention groups at the start of the study.

spans.text: Participants started with 8 weeks on a low energy diet (LED), followed by a weight maintenance period with instructions to follow dietary guidelines in two groups, a moderate protein (MP) and high protein (HP) group.
Participants were randomized into two dietary intervention groups at the start of the study

Dietary intervention groups comprised a moderate protein (MP) group with 15/55/30% of energy from protein/carbohydrate/fat and a moderate dietary glycaemic index (GI) (≥56) and a high protein (HP) group with 25/45/30% of energy from protein/carbohydrate/fat, with a low dietary GI (≤50).

name.value: overweight/obese individuals with impaired fasting glucose and/or impaired glucose tolerance

spans.text: Brain reward reactivity was assessed with functional magnetic resonance imaging in 27 overweight/obese individuals with impaired fasting glucose and/or impaired glucose tolerance (HOMA-IR: 3.7 ± 1.7; BMI: 31.8 ± 3.2 kg/m ; fasting glucose: 6.4 ± 0.6 mmol/L) before and after an 8-week low energy diet followed by a 2-year weight maintenance period, with either high protein (HP) or medium protein (MP) dietary guidelines.

description.value: Functional images were preprocessed with slice-scan-time correction using cubic-spline interpolation, 3D motion correction, temporal high-pass filtering with four cycles, alignment to anatomical images using starting-position and boundary-based registration, and spatial smoothing with a 6 mm FWHM Gaussian filter.
